note.label: The Image of Dysfunction or the Image of God Which One Are You?

precepts.why:
Ezra saw the city of the kingdom with its narrow entrance, “like as if there were a fire on the right hand, and on the left a deep water”. That fire and deep water is the nations afflicting us. Judges makes the point about the nations: “Now these are the nations which the Lord left, to prove Israel by them, even as many of Israel as had not known all the wars of Canaan”.

He didn't get rid of all the nations. He said, no, I'm going to leave something there, because I don't want you to just skate through. You have to learn some things. If we did not have to be buffeted by our enemies, our journey would be quite smooth; but God put it that way because we messed up, and now we have to serve them, and they are going to make it hell for us to get the kingdom.

“Only that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them war, at the least such as before knew nothing thereof”. We didn't know about war before; now we know about war. We are getting the training now. When we get into the kingdom we are going to be experts in everything, bad upon bad, because we will have done it all and endured it all. That is what is going to make us perfect.

Captivity and persecution are hard and rough; nobody wants to go through these things. They can kill the body, but they cannot kill the spirit. They can do all kind of evil to my body physically, but when I come back, I'm going to hang your ass. That is the mindset you have to have: going for the kingdom regardless of what is thrown at you, to persevere between the fire on one side and the deep water on the other. “If then they that live labour not to enter these strait and vain things, they can never receive those that are laid up for them.”

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” The elder world was during the time of Adam. Ezra says “the righteous should inherit these things, but that the ungodly should perish. Nevertheless the righteous shall suffer strait things, and hope for wide”. Strait things is tribulation.

So all Israel is going to go through tribulation, the righteous and the unrighteous. “they that have done wickedly have suffered the strait things, and yet shall not see the wide.” The false prophets say “No evil shall come upon you”, but “a whirlwind of the Lord is gone forth in fury”, and it will not return until he has performed the thoughts of his heart.

What we see on the news, death after death, is just the beginning. A young black girl tied to a tree with a ratchet strap, the kind trucks use to hold down wood, and they call it suicide. Tonya Miller, 27, and Juliana Enza, 16, found hanging from trees, ruled suicides; look at all these names. They can insult our intelligence with this because we are not unified and not connected to the Lord; there is no consequence. They don't do it to the Chinese or Japanese. And it is not only the men: all you independent women, get ready. I don't see color; well, color sees you. It's going to escalate. They won't ask what God you serve: you're in the image of God, and they will come for all the melanated brothers and sisters. The righteous suffer the strait things and hope for the wide.

note.label: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

precepts.why:
Ezra speaks of God “being judge”, and of those “that are cured with his word.” Cured with his word: that is why Christ said, I didn't come for the righteous, I came for the sick, and I am going to give them my word so they can be healed and cured.

Read on and Ezra shows what would happen if God did not forgive those who are cured by his word and put out the multitude of contentions: “There should be very few left peradventure in an innumerable multitude.” Out of all the multitude, hardly any would be left.

So the word of God will cure you; it will heal you. When James says, confess your faults one to another and pray for one another that you may be healed, we have to apply the word of God. That is the cure the physician gives to sinners.

And that is the meaning of “I will have mercy, and not sacrifice.” We used to give sacrifices to absolve us for the sins we committed, but that is not how it was supposed to be from the beginning. The Lord said, I want to see you change rather than keep on sacrificing. His mercy is for those who are cured with his word and actually change.

precepts.point: News read in class: NASA and private companies like SpaceX are advancing plans for a permanent human presence on the moon through the Artemis program, and Artemis 2 just launched. You can have your doubting Thomas saying it is all fake; is it fake like the planes you fly on? A clip of Elon Musk was played discussing colonizing Mars. Why does Esau the Edomite want to go to Mars? Because it is the red planet.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
Amos says they would run to and fro to seek the word of the Lord and not find it. Ezra gives the precept that explains why: “For my son Jesus shall be revealed with those that be with him, and they that remain shall rejoice within four hundred years.” Those with him were the apostles, the followers, the disciples. From Ezra's time to the time of Christ was four hundred years.

“After these years shall my son Christ die, and all men that have life.” Christ was crucified, and all the apostles and all the disciples that followed him either died or were murdered and crucified by Rome. All the men and women that had understanding were dead.

“And the world shall be turned into the old silence seven days, like as in the former judgments: so that no man shall remain.” So that no man that has truth shall remain. From the time after Christ and the disciples died, there was no truth being taught anywhere in the earth. There were no Israelites saying, we are the Israelites and we have to keep the commandments. Instead you had the church fathers, the damn devils, making doctrine, and Tertullian creating the Trinity.

That silence is the famine of hearing the words of the Lord. The world ran to and fro in it for centuries, and that is why the vision had to wait for its appointed time: at the end it shall speak, and not lie.

precepts.point: When Rome came they did not ask who followed Christ; they took the scribes, the Pharisees, the Sadducees and the zealots, and made Josephus a slave. The covenant with hell and death our brothers make with the white man will be broken the same way.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
Ezra says, “the righteous shall suffer strait things, and hope for wide: for they that have done wickedly have suffered the strait things, and yet shall not see the wide.” The strait things are Jacob's trouble, persecution, great tribulation; the wide is the elder world, where Adam dwelt, the kingdom we hope to see on earth. The wicked Israelites will also suffer Jacob's trouble, and yet will not see the kingdom. Zechariah shows how that happened before.

“Three shepherds also I cut off in one month; and my soul lothed them, and their soul also abhorred me.” The three shepherds are the scribes, the Pharisees and the Sadducees. Christ loathed them, and their soul hated him. “Then said I, I will not feed you: that that dieth, let it die; and that that is to be cut off, let it be cut off; and let the rest eat every one the flesh of another.” When did we eat the flesh of one another? 70 AD.

When Rome came, they did not ask, who here follows Christ? We only want you. They took the scribes, the Pharisees, the Sadducees and the Zealots, men, women, boys and girls. Those who stayed behind, if they were not murdered, were enslaved. Josephus was a Pharisee, and they made him a slave; he did not escape. Whatever agreement they had with Rome did them no good.

“And I took my staff, even Beauty, and cut it asunder, that I might break my covenant which I had made with all the people. And it was broken in that day: and so the poor of the flock that waited upon me knew that it was the word of the Lord.” The poor of the flock are the disciples who followed Christ. He told them, when you see Jerusalem compassed with armies, run, and they fled. When it happened they said, that is what Christ was talking about.

The covenant with hell and death that our black and Latin brothers and sisters make with this white man will be broken the same way. It will not do them any good. Jacob's trouble will hit the righteous and the wicked Israelites, all twelve tribes; only the ones who endure to the end will see the wide.

note.label: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

precepts.why:
“That there should not be such heaviness in their destruction, as shall be joy over them that are persuaded to salvation.” We must persuade men to salvation. We see the wars going on with Iran; we see the prophecies coming to pass and escalating. But the Lord told us, go persuade my people to salvation, go bring them into the sanctuary.

How do we do it? Proverbs 25:15: “By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.” To forbear is to patiently restrain. A prince is a very high rank, and with long patience you can persuade even princes. And what does Israel mean? Prince of the power. We have to be patient with the Israelites.

As teachers, be patient and strategic. When you are having that conversation, don't think they are just wicked as hell; they might actually repent, but you were not patient enough. Be diplomatic, learn how to reason. When people come up to you in the street, don't hit them with the first death scripture. You were once in that spot, and the only reason we are in this building is that the Lord opened our eyes.

A soft tongue breaks the bone: somebody can be pissed with you, and you respond with peace. You from Brooklyn, from DC, from PG County, want to respond even more aggressive. But the joy over one of our people persuaded to salvation is greater than the heaviness over the destruction of the rest.

note.label: Christ: the Enemy of Christianity

precepts.why:
Being hated of all nations is not only for those who teach the Bible; Ezra shows who it will affect. “For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” The elder world was paradise in the time of Adam. “If then they that live labour not to enter these strait and vain things, they can never receive those that are laid up for them.”

You have to enter those hard things to enter paradise. The angel is telling Ezra that if we don't go through the hardships of Jacob's trouble, we can never get paradise. If you decide to kill yourself before it happens, you cannot get paradise. If you say, I'm going to join another religion to escape punishment from these other nations, you will never receive it.

Read on: “Nevertheless the righteous shall suffer strait things, and hope for wide”. The righteous shall suffer hard things, that is Jacob's trouble, and hope for paradise. “for they that have done wickedly have suffered the strait things, and yet shall not see the wide.” The wicked Israelites are going through Jacob's trouble too, but they are not going to see the kingdom.

So when Christ said you shall be hated of all nations, it covers all Israel. Whether you teach or not, the strait things are coming; the only question is whether you come out of them into what is laid up for you. That is why you cannot run from the persecution when they command us not to teach in his name.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Ezra is shown “A city is builded, and set upon a broad field, and is full of all good things”, with an entrance so narrow that only one man can go at once. That city is the kingdom of heaven, our inheritance: “Even so also is Israel's portion. Because for their sakes I made the world”. When Adam transgressed, the entrances were made narrow, full of sorrow and travail. But “the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure”. The elder world is the old world, the kingdom of Adam, where all of us were with him, ruling.

Isaiah shows the Lord bringing that back: “And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness, the faithful city.”

As at the first: that is the elder world, when Adam was ruling. There were judges set up then, and the twelve tribes of Israel were set up with him at that time, ruling with him. Were we in the flesh back then? No; we were immortal. As at the beginning: the beginning is Genesis.

So the Lord is not only promising good rulers again. He is promising to restore the government of the old world, the judges and counsellors we had in the beginning, and to call that city the city of righteousness. That is the city full of all good things that Ezra saw, and it is Israel's portion.

precepts.text: Smite the heads of the rulers of the heathen, and gather all the tribes of Jacob together.
precepts.point: After Adam transgressed, the ways became narrow, and Israel must now labour for the inheritance.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“Smite in sunder the heads of the rulers of the heathen, that say, There is none other but we. Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit thou them, as from the beginning.” As from the beginning: so the tribes of Jacob were with the Lord in the beginning, in Genesis.

In Genesis the sons of God were there. When Adam fell, the sons of God were there. There was a government set up, rulership, a kingdom set up with Adam; Adam was not running around naked. There were the gates of Levi, the gates of Benjamin, the gates of Manasses: all twelve tribes in the beginning with the Lord, in their spiritual bodies. People ask what tribe Abraham was from, what tribe Isaac was from. The twelve tribes were always there. When Moses says the sons of God, that is the twelve tribes.

“O Lord, have mercy upon the people that is called by thy name, and upon Israel, whom thou hast named thy firstborn.” We are named God's firstborn because he created us first, before the world began. “O be merciful unto Jerusalem, thy holy city, the place of thy rest”, and “Give testimony unto those that thou hast possessed from the beginning, and raise up prophets that have been in thy name.”

In these last days God has raised up the prophets that have been in his name. The prophets of old are back, in the tribes of Israel, in this building.

precepts.text: God made not death, and the generations of the world were healthful.
precepts.point: After Adam transgressed, the ways became narrow, and Israel must now labour for the inheritance.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
The entrances of the elder world “were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” Wisdom shows what that world was like: “For God made not death: neither hath he pleasure in the destruction of the living. For he created all things, that they might have their being: and the generations of the world were healthful; and there is no poison of destruction in them, nor the kingdom of death upon the earth”.

The generations of the world were healthful: we were living forever. There was no poison of destruction in us and no kingdom of death. The kingdom of death was established after Adam fell, when Satan was given power over this earth and began ruling it, him and his children. The kingdom of death is the white man and Satan ruling the earth. Before that was the kingdom of Adam, the kingdom of heaven. That is why Moses could promise “the days of heaven upon the earth”: he saw Adam rule.

“For righteousness is immortal”: keep God's laws and you live forever. “But ungodly men with their works and words called it to them: for when they thought to have it their friend, they consumed to nought, and made a covenant with it”. A lot of our people have made a covenant with death, worshipping Satan and living in the kingdom of death. That is why the last thing Christ has to conquer is death, and then there will be no more death, period.

note.label: Numbers 23: How Shall I Curse, Whom God Hath Not Cursed?

precepts.why:
Hath He spoken, and shall He not make it good? Esdras tried asking the Most High to spare the wicked for the prayers of the righteous, and was told to concern himself with the righteous. “This present life is not the end where much glory doth abide; therefore have they prayed for the weak.”

“But the day of doom shall be the end of this time, and the beginning of the immortality for to come, wherein corruption is past, Intemperance is at an end, infidelity is cut off, righteousness is grown, and truth is sprung up. Then shall no man be able to save him that is destroyed, nor to oppress him that hath gotten the victory.” In the day of doom no man shall be able to save him that is destroyed; the sentence stands for ever.

This present life is not the end, and asking the righteous to pray for those that outright despise God and His laws is praying for the weak. That is what we doubted back in Deuteronomy when Moses read the curses over us; we thought the Lord would not make good on His word. But the Lord is longsuffering and patient and will in no wise acquit the wicked; we will not escape our sins.

precepts.text: The entrance is narrow, set in a dangerous place with fire on the right hand and deep water on the left, one only path between them for one man to walk.
precepts.point: Ephraim being the firstborn means Israel is the firstborn of the Most High, set higher than the kings of the earth, who are the other nations, so all of Israel shall be over all the nations; the reason Ephraim was singled out is the tribes were not the first tribe that came, but the promise is to all Israel.

note.label: Jeremiah 31: The New Covenant

precepts.why:
The straight way the Lord leads Israel in is not a wide one. Ezra describes it: “The entrance thereof is narrow, and is set in a dangerous place to fall, like as if there were a fire on the right hand, and on the left a deep water”.

“And one only path between them both, even between the fire and the water, so small that there could but one man go there at once.” Fire on the right hand, deep water on the left, and one only path between them for one man to walk. That is the straight way of Jeremiah 31:9, keeping God's laws, wherein they shall not stumble because he leads them by the rivers of waters.

precepts.text: The way to the city is narrow, set in a dangerous place, and but one man only can go therein at once.
precepts.point: They shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God. They come from the four corners because they were scattered to the four corners.

note.label: Luke 13: Except Ye Repent, and the Strait Gate

precepts.why:
The strait gate is pictured for Ezra: “A city is builded, and set upon a broad field, and is full of all good things: The entrance thereof is narrow, and is set in a dangerous place to fall, like as if there were a fire on the right hand, and on the left a deep water: And one only path between them both, even between the fire and the water, so small that there could but one man go there at once.”

The strait way is a narrow one, set in a dangerous place, and but one man only can go therein at once. It is walked by discipline: correction, falling, getting back up, and correcting yourself. Many will seek to enter in and shall not be able; many hear this word and turn back to the world rather than walk it.

precepts.text: Both the righteous and the wicked suffer strait things, but only the righteous receive the reward.
precepts.point: Properly prepare your mind, because anything can happen at any moment and you must be ready to drop everything and leave. In the world men drove drunk and gang-banged unafraid of death, so do not now be a coward for the truth; the Most High controls death, and it is better to die for this truth than to die for nothing.

note.label: Acts 9: A Chosen Vessel

precepts.why:
“Nevertheless the righteous shall suffer strait things, and hope for wide: for they that have done wickedly have suffered the strait things, and yet shall not see the wide.” Both the righteous and the wicked suffer strait things, but only the righteous receive the reward.

Saul suffered them here. The Jews watched the gates day and night to kill him, and the disciples let him down by the wall in a basket by night. This is what you are in: your front door may be occupied and you may have to go down the window on a rope. Properly prepare your mind, because anything can happen at any moment and you must be ready to drop everything and leave.

In the world men drove drunk and gang-banged unafraid of death, so do not now be a coward for the truth. The Most High controls death, and it is better to die for this truth than to die for nothing; the wicked suffer the strait things too, and they shall not see the wide.

note.label: HELP | Healing Emotionally Lost People

precepts.why:
What is the darkness of 2 Esdras 7:55? “Arise, shine; for thy light is come”: the Lord’s Christ is come, “and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.” That is what we have to see in you, brothers: the glory of the Lord, not that blackness and darkness.

“For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth”: the earth is covered with pornography, lasciviousness, all kinds of sin and evil. “And gross darkness the people”: the earth is in darkness, but our people are in gross darkness, total darkness, no light. Esau has us thinking we are nothing, good for nothing, to be raised in the ghetto and the projects. Not knowing who you are, not knowing that God and Christ look like you, not knowing what to do to come out of the conditions your people are in, killing your brother who looks just like you, stealing from your own people: that is gross darkness, sin covering our people.

“But the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee.” That is why we march and go into the highways and hedges and the corners: not for vain glory, but because God commands us to, so that people see the light and there is no longer gross darkness. note.label: America and the World Will Pay Reparations

“The same must know it after death by pain.” There is pain after death for those spirits that reject and hate God’s law. Y’all keep on playing.

note.label: Standing Tall When The Smoke Clears

precepts.why:
This is speaking of how we are going to obtain immortality and eternal life. “The entrance thereof is narrow”: it is not easy, it is a strict walk, “and is set in a dangerous place to fall, like as if there were a fire on the right hand, and on the left a deep water”. We are walking through perilous times. In these last days the most wicked kingdom on earth is ruling the whole earth, and we have sin and lust all around us and within us. Fire on one side and deep water on the other means there is very little margin for error.

“And one only path between them both, even between the fire and the water, so small that there could but one man go there at once.” That means you can’t save nobody but yourself. You have to endure and fight. You can’t ride into the kingdom on anybody else’s coattail. That’s my officer, that’s my counsel of a thousand: but do you listen to the counsel? Do you apply it? You are not getting the kingdom because you have a righteous counsellor of a thousand. You have to apply yourself.

“If this city now were given unto a man for an inheritance, if he never shall pass the danger set before it, how shall he receive this inheritance?” That danger is the suffering, the pain and the tribulation. “Even so also is Israel’s portion.” That is our portion, our plight.

“Because for their sakes I made the world: and when Adam transgressed my statutes, then was decreed that now is done.” Everything was given to Adam; immortality was given to them. But when Adam transgressed, “Then were the entrances of this world made narrow, full of sorrow and travail”. In this truth there will be sorrow and travail. “They are but few and evil”: few and evil days. Full of perils, which is trouble in all its variations, “and very painful.”

note.label: Standing Tall When The Smoke Clears

precepts.why:
“This is the condition of the battle, which man that is born upon the earth shall fight”. The whole Bible is telling you over and over that you have to fight. It’s narrow; it’s fire on one side and deep water on the other; it’s battle; this is war. It tells you over and over to prepare you mentally for what’s to come. All of us are going to fight.

“That, if he be overcome, he shall suffer as thou hast said”: if you get overcome by the sorrow, by your lust, your temptation, your sin, if you faint in the day of persecution, you are going to suffer as God said. “But if he get the victory, he shall receive the thing that I say.” That is the kingdom.

note.label: THE REWARD OF THE RIGHTEOUS: WHO IS REALLY GETTING IN?

precepts.why:
“A city is builded, and set upon a broad field, and is full of all good things”: that city is the kingdom. “The entrance thereof is narrow”, between a fire and a deep water, “so small that there could but one man go there at once.” You cannot go for your children or your spouse; you have to go for yourself. We are the ones who have to pass the danger; through much tribulation we enter the kingdom. What are they going through? Nothing. They are oppressing us.

“Even so also is Israel’s portion.” The whole thing is Israel's portion, the trials, the one path and the kingdom itself. “Because for their sakes I made the world”: about nobody else but us. When Adam transgressed, the entrances were made narrow, “full of sorrow and travail”.

“Nevertheless the righteous shall suffer strait things, and hope for wide: for they that have done wickedly have suffered the strait things, and yet shall not see the wide.” Be wicked and you go through the trials too, and they will kill you the same way they kill us, but you will not see the kingdom. It behooves you to repent, stop being prideful, go by what the scripture says and hope for the wide. “There be many that perish in this life, because they despise the law of God”: God gave plain commandments, what to do to live and what to observe to avoid punishment. Keep the commandments and live; break them and you die.

“The faces of them which have used abstinence shall shine above the stars”: those who refrain themselves from sin. “For while we lived and committed iniquity, we considered not that we should begin to suffer for it after death.” “This is the condition of the battle, which man that is born upon the earth shall fight”: if he gets the victory and overcomes, “he shall receive the thing that I say”, the kingdom that is for him. It is for us.

note.label: The 4 Temples In Jerusalem

precepts.why:
“For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” We are going back to the elder world: the elder world is the kingdom, paradise. “If then they that live labour not to enter these strait and vain things, they can never receive those that are laid up for them.”

“Thou hast ordained in thy law, that the righteous should inherit these things, but that the ungodly should perish. Nevertheless the righteous shall suffer strait things, and hope for wide”. We are going to suffer hard things, affliction, and hope for the wide: the kingdom. “For they that have done wickedly have suffered the strait things, and yet shall not see the wide.” Our people who have done wickedly suffer too, and will not see immortality, the kingdom. That is overcoming to inherit all things.

note.label: Must Be Hated To Be Heard! The Price Of Speaking Truth To Modern Day Christians

precepts.why:
Because they are two-time losers, they want us to be losers too. But the kingdom is for us and only us.

“For what profit is it for men now in this present time to live in heaviness, and after death to look for punishment?” What profit is it for us to live in hell right now, getting up for our nine to fives while the white man oppresses our people and kills us in the streets? Who gets the true punishment? Our enemies get the punishment for what they have done to us. That is why they want to keep us in sin, teach us a false Christ, and say the laws are done away with: they know they are going into captivity and will be destroyed, and they want to take us down with them.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why: “And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her”. Don’t worry about the dead. A lot of times our mind wonders, what about those of us who have died in this truth? Don’t worry about them; they too shall be restored. “And so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed unto them.” So everything’s going to be restored.

note.label: THE DECEPTION OF SIN

precepts.why:
Ezra says the exact same thing. “This is the condition of the battle, which man that is born upon the earth shall fight; That, if he be overcome, he shall suffer as thou hast said: but if he get the victory, he shall receive the thing that I say.”

“For this is the life whereof Moses spake unto the people while he lived, saying, Choose thee life, that thou mayest live.” Ezra takes us back to what Moses said. The Bible is very redundant: everything connects and is attached to one another. Ezra equates life and death with righteousness and unrighteousness, keeping the commandments of God and not keeping them.

So do you have a choice whether or not to be in the battle, whether or not to deal with the terms and conditions set before us? No. You are here, you are breathing, you see everything in front of you, but you have a choice to make. The Bible says there are people who will see, hear, understand and still decide to follow this world. Like the white girl in the movie who hears the growling, gets up and walks right over to where the danger is: you knew death was afoot and you still went that direction. We don't know what anybody will do until the last breath is gone from them; somebody can be a complete demon and turn their life around. But this puts us in the perspective of how God really is, not a fairy-tale imagination of him. Crying and boohooing in church doesn't mean God is near you; Buddhists and Muslims cry too. You are just emotional, all up in your mind, and nothing about it is biblical.

note.label: THE DECEPTION OF SIN

precepts.why:
“When Adam transgressed my statutes, then was decreed that now is done.” When Adam transgressed, things were made the way they are now. Above this Ezra speaks of the dangers of reaching the glorious, beautiful city and the beautiful sea: to get there you have to go through a narrow path, the only way, and a dangerous road. It became that way when Adam transgressed.

“Then were the entrances of this world made narrow, full of sorrow and travail: they are but few and evil.” The entrances are life. The path we all must walk became difficult; before, we were going to live forever and weren't worried about anything. Now we have a short life, and that short life is full of evil. Terrible things happen all through it, and if you thought that was something, wait until the next thing hits you.

“For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit. If then they that live labour not to enter these strait and vain things, they can never receive those that are laid up for them.” If you don't go through that narrow and strait gate, you won't inherit eternal life and the heavenly mansions Christ told us are coming if we endure. You have to go through all the dangers and make it through; you won't coast. Many of us think that once we wake up to who we are it will be easy. No, that is when Satan comes for you. You didn't have these problems when you were in the world; it turns up when you come into this truth.

note.label: THE DECEPTION OF SIN

precepts.why:
Ezra gets to the root of things. “O thou Adam, what hast thou done? for though it was thou that sinned, thou art not fallen alone, but we all that come of thee.”

“It had been better not to have given the earth unto Adam.” Why does Ezra say this? He is looking at the end result of what happened. Little by little the scriptures show what went down in the garden: Adam was given dominion over everything. “Or else, when it was given him, to have restrained him from sinning.” This is Ezra in his man mind trying to come up with a solution to the problem of man: you could have made Adam so that he could not sin.

“For what profit is it for men now in this present time to live in heaviness, and after death to look for punishment?” Heaviness in this life, and then die and look for punishment. “For what profit is it unto us, if there be promised us an immortal time, whereas we have done the works that bring death?” He is doing the same thing Paul did, showing the fight between the flesh and the spirit, because in this life all men are messing up. Ezra doesn't even realize he is asking for a savior, and we needed one, because there was no coming back from there.

“And that the glory of the most High is kept to defend them which have led a wary life, whereas we have walked in the most wicked ways of all?” Ezra was righteous, but he was real about himself, and he equates himself with those who fall short. Many of us act like we can't believe it when someone messes up, when we all fall short. We all live the same life, battle the same flesh and deal with the same thoughts; Ezra just recognized it.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 2 Message to the 7 Churches

precepts.why: “But his law have they despised, and denied his covenants; in his statutes have they not been faithful, and have not performed his works.” His works are bound to his law, covenants and statutes. Keeping Christ's works to the end means remaining faithful in these things, not inventing a religion in which obedience no longer matters.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 21 Thy Kingdom Come

precepts.why: To explain his works. “But his law have they despised, and denied his covenants; in his statutes have they not been faithful, and have not performed his works”: so his works refers to his law, his statutes, his covenant.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 21 Thy Kingdom Come

precepts.why: “Because for their sakes I made the world”: the world was made for us. That’s what we all have to understand.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
“Enter ye in at the strait gate.” This is the same path Ezra was shown; that is where Christ got it from. The same strait gate, the same straight path between the fire and the water.

“For wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction.” If you are not facing any difficulties, trials or tribulations while keeping these laws and commandments, you are going through that wide gate, and you ain’t making it. This truth is not easy. It is going to be hard, and it is going to get harder as time goes on. Watch the news: the white man is starting to revert to what he was in the 60s, 50s, 40s, back through the 1800s and 1700s. The smile he had on his face when he saw a Negro is starting to fade. And black folks are not prepared for it, because when they see him they see God. He can sit there and speak his hate to their face, and they say, he’s just angry, he’s going through things, come let me hug you. That’s the apologist.

The man who passed away, that white folks are losing their minds over, talked crazy about black folks: he spoke evil about Martin Luther King and said black people are violent, and black folks are crying over him, saying we lost a good one. You are the ones going through the wide gate. And the Lord had it where he suffered the very violence he spoke of. God is a very ironic God; he does things to remind you, don’t talk about his people too much.

“Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.” Why few? Because black folks do not want the hard; they want the easy, instant gratification. The other nations deal with longevity: they do things knowing it will affect us 100, 200, 300, 400 years down the line; they have plan A, and if A fails they have B and C set already. Black folks have no plan at all: do or die. They don’t want difficulty, accountability, reality, responsibility. Men will teach that the men of the Bible were free and had rulership, but won’t teach how to go about it: be warmed and filled. When it comes to ignorance, chaos and stupidity, black people and brown people find safe haven among themselves. White folks labelled their own and said, that’s not all of us; black folks call ill behaviour culture and heritage, a black thing. No, it is a slave thing, a slave-minded thing.

Few find that straight path, because it is easier to do nothing and expect God to do everything: keep no laws, no commandments, do whatever I want and just believe, and I’m good. That is the wide gate.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
“My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” That goes back to the straight path, the fire and the water, the perils, dangers, sorrows and travails. “Set thy heart aright”: set your mind right, “and constantly endure” that straight path, the trouble, Jacob’s trouble that is coming. “And make not haste in time of trouble”: don’t get weak, don’t run. This truth is blood in, blood out; there is no running from it. Christ died for you; we owe him. There is nowhere to go.

“Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end. Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate.”

“For gold is tried in the fire.” Fire is twofold: a cleaning instrument and a destructive instrument. It does both. “And acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.” Adversity goes back to the strait things, troubling times. You will lose your family, your friends, your children. Some will lose their jobs, their homes, those closest to them, and many of us are going to lose our lives here when things get real bad. The church is the people, not the building, and many of us are going to be faced with a choice. That is why acceptable men are tried in the furnace of adversity.

The Lord referred to Egypt as the iron furnace, and that is where we are now: America is a spiritual Egypt, and it is the iron furnace too. You are either going to go through this fire and come out better, or you are going to burn along with it.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
“But the Lord hath taken you, and brought you forth out of the iron furnace, even out of Egypt.” He called literal Egypt the iron furnace: hot misery, affliction, persecution. We went through all of that in Egypt, and likewise we will do so in Egypt again, here.

Egypt is called the iron furnace because acceptable men are going to go through that fire, “to be unto him a people of inheritance.”

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
“For they be thy people, and thine inheritance, which thou broughtest forth out of Egypt, from the midst of the furnace of iron.” We are back in the iron furnace, and they are heating it.

A furnace takes a while to get hot. In the civil rights era the furnace was cooling down some: black folks got jobs, joined unions, used the white man’s toilet, sat at the front of the bus, and thought we made it. No: the furnace is getting hot now. White folks are being real honest now. They call it climate change, global warming; that is exactly what it is, and only black folks are still in it. They call it ICE; they should call it fire. The northern kingdom is getting dragged in the street, and they damn sure don’t feel no ice. You feeling it now? The iron furnace.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
“But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and there shall no torment touch them.” Deacon Isaac said it best: when they leave this world, they mourn for us, because they are in paradise. Their leaving is sad for us, not for them; they are in a better place, and we are in the worst place to be. No torment touches them; the torment awaits us.

“In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die”: in the sight of the wicked, the heathen, even our people, they seem to be killed, murdered off. “And their departure is taken for misery,” because there will be torture going on, “and their going from us to be utter destruction: but they are in peace.” They are at rest. “For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality”: back to that builded city.

“And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded.” God calls torture and death a little chastisement. A little. “For God proved them, and found them worthy for himself. As gold in the furnace hath he tried them,” and the iron furnace is here, “and received them as a burnt offering,” because they got killed.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
“Two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.” Many of us are going to die, especially here in America; a lot of us are going to be destroyed entirely.

“And I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried.” Tried in the iron furnace: the iron furnace called captivity, and the iron furnace called a body. This fleshly body is a damn furnace too. “They shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, The Lord is my God.”

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
“And I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin.” What is he talking about? The dross and the tin are all the impurities, and he takes all that away.

“Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil.” That goes back to being reformed, being refined in the fire, so that the acceptable come through.

note.label: BORN IN FIRE & WATER

precepts.why:
“Then shall they be known, who are my chosen; and they shall be tried as the gold in the fire.” Then it will be known who are the chosen, who are worthy: those tried as gold in the fire, as the psalmist said.

The baby is preserved in the fire and in the water; the path set before us is fire and water; and the chosen are tried by fire. That is the fire. Next comes the water.
